about:
Waterbury Electronic Supply operates from Waterbury, Connecticut The company has been in business since 1995 and is led by Ron Hapken, Matt Hapken, and Pat Hapken. It began as a franchised distributor of quality electronic parts and components, aiming to bring value to every customer.

The firm distributes a broad line of electronic components including connectors, relays, switches, potentiometers, power supplies, enclosures, displays, and more. It also offers value‑added services such as sheet metal fabrication and off‑shore PCB supply chain services with quick turnaround and production. Custom enclosure design is available through the BOXCAD online tool, and the company holds ISO 9001:2015 certification.

Waterbury Electronic Supply serves customers in industries that require electronic components, such as industrial automation, telecommunications, medical devices, and general electronics manufacturing. Its franchised distributor status means it supplies parts from recognized manufacturers.

The company states its guiding principles: treating customers and suppliers as they would want to be treated, delivering customer value through quality parts, fair pricing, and excellent service, doing everything possible to help customers, and supporting customers' cost‑saving initiatives.

The shop provides metal fabrication and welding services, including on-site welding, custom metalwork, and sheet metal fabrication. It also offers complete crane rental services—boom trucks, hydraulic cranes, and hoists—for construction and heavy-lifting needs. The facility sits just off Highway 77 with ample space for custom projects and on-site sheet metal storage. Headcount and annual volumes are not disclosed.

Customers range from residential homeowners needing benches, ladders, or rebar cages for elevator shafts to commercial contractors in the construction industry. The company welcomes walk-in clients without prepared blueprints and serves both Surry and Wilkes counties as well as the broader Foothills region.

Watson Metals emphasizes its local ownership, personalized service, and three decades in business as differentiators. On-site welding availability and the ability to assist clients from concept to completion without formal drawings are highlighted as key reasons customers choose them.

name: Wayne Wire
old_description: Since 1943, Wayne Wire Cloth Products has been the trusted supplier of high-quality filtration components to Fortune 500 companies worldwide.
about:
Wayne Wire Cloth Products, Inc. was founded in 1943 in Wayne, Michigan, and established its headquarters in Kalkaska, Michigan in 1950. The company was purchased by its current owners in 1996 and has since expanded to manufacturing operations in Hillman, Michigan, and Juarez, Mexico.

The company produces precision wire cloth and filtration components, including expanded foil mesh, custom fabricated assemblies, welded and brazed parts, and machined components. Its capabilities span manual and automated pressing, rolling, convolution, shearing, TIG/MIG/resistance welding, silver and nickel/gold brazing, vacuum furnace brazing, ultrasonic cleaning, and comprehensive inspection. The company operates manufacturing facilities in Kalkaska and Hillman, Michigan, and Juarez, Mexico, supporting both prototype and high-volume production.

Wayne Wire serves aerospace and defense (NADCAP and AS9100D certified), automotive and transportation (including Tier 1 suppliers and supplemental restraint systems), medical devices, HVAC and refrigeration, water systems, and energy sectors. Its customer base includes Fortune 500 companies worldwide.

The company emphasizes zero-defect manufacturing for safety-critical components, rapid prototyping for design validation, and a quality management system built on 80-plus years of precision manufacturing experience.

name: Wei Chuan USA
old_description: For over five decades, Wei-Chuan USA's passion for delicious food has allowed our customers to enjoy authentic Chinese flavors: every recipe balances tradition with innovation to make meals that everyone can enjoy.
about:
Wei Chuan USA was founded in 1972 in Los Angeles, California, by brothers Thomas and Robert Huang, who had recently immigrated from Taiwan and missed the authentic flavors of home. The company’s name, meaning “comprehensive flavors” in Chinese, reflects its mission to bridge cultures through food. Headquarters are now located in Murfreesboro, Tennessee.

The company operates two USDA Grant of Inspection and FDA-approved manufacturing facilities — one in Los Angeles and a second established in Tennessee in 2006 — both running certified HACCP, GMP, and SSOP programs. Its product lines span gyoza, potstickers, spring rolls, egg rolls, buns, dumplings, wontons, wrappers, entrée items, shumai, natural and organic selections, groceries, and food-service packs. An in-house R&D team of food scientists, nutritionists, and chefs develops and tests every recipe.

Wei Chuan serves retail grocery chains, food-service distributors, and consumers across North America. Its Food Service and Groceries categories supply restaurants, institutions, and supermarkets, while the Natural, Organic, and Vegetarian line targets health-conscious shoppers. The Dumpling King series, launched in the early 1990s, remains a flagship retail product.

The founders started the business because authentic Chinese flavors were unavailable in the U.S. market. Today, Wei Chuan emphasizes continuous investment in technology, rigorous quality control, and recipes that balance tradition with innovation, aiming to make “comprehensive flavors” accessible to every household.

about:
Welding Shop Mfg LLC operates from Cheyenne, Wyoming, where it was founded in 1975 as The Welding Shop by Gerald (Jerry) and JoAnn Pauli. The business remains family-owned and operated, now led by their sons Gary and Dwayne Pauli.

The shop provides welding, custom fabrication, and aluminum welding services, along with machine work, drive shaft repair, hydraulic equipment repair, and ornamental metal work such as hand rails and safety window guards. Since 2000 it has manufactured its own line of Paulibuilt trailers for recreational and commercial use, and since 2012 it has stocked a large inventory of trailer parts and accessories. Mobile welding services are also offered, and the facility maintains a sizable supply of iron and steel for customer projects.

Customers include trailer owners in both recreational and commercial transportation, construction firms needing custom ornamental metalwork, industrial maintenance operations requiring machine and hydraulic repairs, and the railroad industry — one testimonial notes the shop's welders outperforming railroad welders.

The company emphasizes customer service, honesty, integrity, and reliability, with a motto of “FOR ALL YOUR WELDING & TRAILER NEEDS.” It aims to handle jobs of any size with fast, friendly service and the ability to custom-build trailers to exact specifications.

name: Wesco Electrical Supply
old_description: Since 1922 Wesco has been the leading electrical products and solutions provider. Electrification has and will continue to change the world with digitalization, green energy and grid modernization only accelerating change.
about:
Wesco Electrical Supply was founded in 1922 and is headquartered in Bangor, Maine. The company began as an electrical products provider and has grown into a global distributor of electrical, communications, and utility supplies. It operates as a publicly traded corporation, ranked on the Fortune 500, with no single family or veteran ownership indicated in public records.

Today Wesco distributes more than 1.5 million products across over 50 countries, serving 150,000 customers with a workforce of approximately 20,000 employees. Its service portfolio includes project coordination and forecasting, grid hardening solutions, program management, regular hardware inspections, ground assembly rotation, and security hardware supply. The company emphasizes supply chain services and continuous improvement culture to manage complex customer requirements.

Wesco’s customer base spans communications and networking, power generation and distribution, electrical and lighting, and security sectors. It also supports emerging markets such as battery energy storage systems and AI-driven edge computing infrastructure. Typical buyers include utilities, contractors, industrial facilities, and commercial construction firms.

Recognition such as Fortune’s World’s Most Admired Companies listing, AIQ 75 ranking, and Great Place to Work certification reflect its stated focus on operational excellence and employee engagement.

about:
Founded in 2005 in Tarpon Springs, Florida, West Florida Components operates as an online distributor of electronic components. The company is now part of Supply Shield, with its warehouse located in St. Petersburg, Florida, and is not open to the public.

The company stocks a wide range of electronic components across categories including semiconductors, capacitors, diodes, transistors, resistors, enclosures, and hardware. It emphasizes an in-stock guarantee—only advertising parts physically present in its warehouse—and offers same-day shipping for orders paid by 1 PM. The catalog also includes vintage parts and clearance items.

West Florida Components serves hobbyists, educators, and professionals seeking electronic components for projects, prototyping, and repair, with a focus on obsolete and hard-to-find parts. Its online catalog includes learning resources such as component glossaries, datasheets, and project guides, supporting both novice and experienced builders.

The company differentiates itself by specializing in obsolete and hard-to-find electronic parts, maintaining a strict in-stock policy, and providing toll-free customer support. During its transition to Supply Shield, it requires a minimum order of $150 and directs customers to phone-based ordering.

name: West Hartford Solar
old_description: West Hartford Solar was founded by Dan Hovey with one simple mission: to make solar accessible, personal and ethical. What started as a solo journey has grown into a regional team serving customers throughout New England.
about:
West Hartford Solar operates from West Hartford, Connecticut. The company was founded by Dan Hovey, who serves as owner and principal consultant, with a mission to make solar energy accessible, personal, and ethical. What began as a solo endeavor has expanded into a regional team serving customers across New England.

The firm functions as a licensed solar installer managing projects from design and permitting through installation and activation. It maintains installation crews in Connecticut and supplements coverage in Massachusetts through a partnership with Earthlight Technologies and in New York through New York State Solar Farm. The team includes senior consultants covering western Massachusetts, the Connecticut River Valley, southeastern Connecticut, and the northwestern hills.

Customers range from homeowners seeking to reduce energy costs to businesses, schools, nonprofits, and municipalities pursuing long-term sustainability goals. The company coordinates custom solar solutions for corporate facilities, housing authorities, and local government projects across Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New York.

Hovey started the business to provide transparent pricing, personalized guidance, and a stress-free experience, emphasizing honesty and responsiveness at every step. The company highlights access to multiple financing options and a commitment to tailoring each system to the specific property rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach.

name: West Tennessee Solar Exhibit
old_description: More than 25 acres contain a solar array of approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic solar panels. Electricity generated is distributed through purchase agreements with local utility Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and Tennessee Valley Authority.
about:
The West Tennessee Solar Exhibit operates a utility-scale solar farm and an interactive educational center known as SPECTRUM on a 25-acre site in Stanton, Tennessee. The project originated in 2009 when a $62.5-million allocation from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act was awarded to the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development. The University of Tennessee Research Foundation was contracted to oversee creation and operation of the facility, which was designed and built by Signal Energy, LLC of Chattanooga in 2011, with grid connection achieved in early 2012.

The farm comprises approximately 21,000 fixed-tilt, ground-mounted photovoltaic panels generating electricity sold under purchase agreements to Chickasaw Electric Cooperative and the Tennessee Valley Authority. Alongside power production, the SPECTRUM exhibit provides hands-on learning stations, games, and QR-linked resources to teach solar energy basics to students, homeowners, and business visitors. The exhibit partners include Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and multiple state agencies.

The facility serves utilities, educational institutions, and the general public. Its electricity feeds the regional grid through TVA and Chickasaw Electric Cooperative, while the exhibit attracts school groups, science-fair participants, and homeowners exploring rooftop solar. Partners such as the U.S. Department of Energy, Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council, and Volkswagen reflect a broad stakeholder base spanning government, research, and industry.

The project was conceived as a dual-purpose asset: a revenue-generating solar array and a public showcase for renewable energy technology. Its backers emphasized job creation, education, and technology commercialization as core goals, positioning the site as a living laboratory for solar adoption in Tennessee.
